questions.q: Per this lesson, why does caching matter more in pure dollar terms for AI apps than for a typical CRUD API?
options: A call to an LLM provider costs real, metered money and can take seconds, unlike a cheap, fast database call
AI apps never make database calls at all
Caching is only possible for AI apps, not for other kinds of APIs
LLM providers charge a flat monthly fee regardless of usage
questions.explain: A cache hit on an AI call isn't just faster -- it's a metered call you simply don't pay for, which is a bigger deal than for a near-free database read.

questions.q: What is the main limitation of exact-match response caching, according to this lesson?
options: It cannot be implemented for any API
It only works for RAG-style applications
It catches only identical repeats, which is narrow since users rarely phrase the same question the same way twice
It requires storing the entire model's weights
questions.explain: Exact-match is simple but narrow -- it misses the common case where two users ask the same thing in different words.

questions.q: How does semantic caching decide whether a new prompt can reuse a cached response?
options: It requires the new prompt's text to match a stored prompt character-for-character
It compares the new prompt's embedding against stored prompts' embeddings for similarity
It always reuses the most recently cached response regardless of content
It checks whether the user's account ID matches a cached user
questions.explain: Semantic caching embeds the new prompt and compares it to stored prompt embeddings -- similar enough, and the cached response is reused.

questions.q: What does a retrieval cache store, in a RAG-style application, per this lesson?
options: The user's full conversation history across all sessions
The model's weights, cached between deployments
The raw HTTP request headers for auditing
The retrieved context/documents for a query, separately from the final generated answer
questions.explain: A retrieval cache is specific to RAG apps: it caches the retrieved context used to generate an answer, as a separate thing from the answer itself.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call a stale semantic-cache hit a harder bug to catch than an obvious error?
options: Because stale cache hits always return an HTTP error code
Because the response reads as fluent and on-topic, while actually being wrong because the underlying data moved on
Because semantic caches are disabled by default in most frameworks
Because stale responses are always shorter than fresh ones, making them easy to spot
questions.explain: A stale cached answer doesn't look broken -- it's coherent and plausible, which is exactly what makes it dangerous without deliberate invalidation rules.
